garden-rooms.title: Bespoke Garden Rooms in Lancashire | Tom Cutts
garden-rooms.description: Bespoke garden rooms and home offices in Colne, Clitheroe and the Ribble Valley. Explore layout, finishes and decking with Tom Cutts. Request a free quote.
garden-rooms.h1: Bespoke garden rooms, built around your life.
intro: Give work, exercise or hobbies a space of their own. Tom Cutts Joinery & Building creates bespoke garden rooms for homeowners in Colne, Pendle, the Ribble Valley and surrounding areas. We start with how you want to use the room, then work through the layout, materials and practical details together.

Your garden room should make sense for both your home and your garden. With 18+ years of hands-on construction and management experience, Tom brings building knowledge and careful joinery to the project, from the structure through to the finishing details.

sections.heading: Start with what the room needs to do
paragraphs: For a home office, think about desk space, daylight, sockets and the route back to the house. A gym needs a layout that suits your equipment; a studio may need more wall space or storage. Tell us what matters most so the footprint, doors and windows support the way you will actually use the room.

sections.heading: Discuss comfort, services and finishes early
paragraphs: We discuss insulation, ventilation, glazing and the internal finish as part of the specification. Power, lighting, heating and internet requirements should also be considered before the work begins. This gives us a clear picture of the associated trades and preparation your project needs, rather than leaving essential details to the end.

sections.heading: Connect the room to your garden
paragraphs: Decking can create a useful place to sit outside the room and help connect the entrance with the rest of the garden. Planning both together lets us consider steps, changes in level and routes around the building. We can also discuss a pergola or bespoke outdoor joinery as part of the wider space.

sections.heading: A quotation based on your actual site
paragraphs: Size is only one part of a garden-room quotation. Access, the existing ground, preparation, materials and services all affect the work involved. Share photographs, approximate dimensions, your postcode and a preferred budget. We can then discuss a site visit and prepare a quotation with a clear scope. Required permissions and professional input should be resolved before construction starts.

faqs.q: Can a garden room be designed for use throughout the year?
faqs.a: Yes, that can be part of the brief. Tell us when and how you intend to use it so we can discuss insulation, glazing, ventilation and heating requirements. The agreed specification will set out what is included.

faqs.q: Can you build decking at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes. A combined project lets us plan the entrance, outdoor seating, steps and connection to the house together. We can also quote for decking as a separate project.

faqs.q: Do I need a finished design before getting in touch?
faqs.a: No. An idea of the room’s purpose, approximate size and budget is enough to begin. Photos showing the proposed position and access to the garden are particularly useful.

faqs.q: How much will my garden room cost?
faqs.a: We quote for the individual project. The size, specification, ground preparation, access and required services all influence the price. Contact Tom for a free, no-obligation discussion and quotation for the agreed work.

decking.title: Decking Installation in Lancashire | Tom Cutts
decking.description: Timber and composite decking for gardens across Colne, Pendle and the Ribble Valley. Discuss steps, seating and garden-room connections. Get a free quote.
decking.h1: Decking that makes more of your garden.
intro: Create a place to sit, eat and spend time outdoors. Tom Cutts Joinery & Building installs decking for homes across Colne, Pendle, Clitheroe, Whalley and the surrounding area. Whether you want a defined seating space or a deck outside a new garden room, we help turn the idea into a practical layout.

We look at how the deck will meet the house, garden and existing levels before discussing the finish. The result starts with a clear plan for the whole space, supported by Tom’s background in joinery, building and project management.

sections.heading: Choose a layout for everyday use
paragraphs: Think about where your table, chairs and other furniture will sit, and leave room to move around them. A deck also needs to work with doors, paths and access to the rest of the garden. We can discuss steps, edges and changes in level so the layout feels considered from every approach.

sections.heading: Compare timber and composite finishes
paragraphs: Timber and composite boards offer different looks and care requirements. We discuss the appearance you want, your budget and the product options suitable for the job. Board colour, direction, edging and visible fixings all contribute to the finished space. Ask us to explain the proposed specification and maintenance expectations before you make your choice.

sections.heading: Look beneath the finished boards
paragraphs: A decking project involves more than choosing the surface. Existing ground, support, drainage, access and any removal work affect the scope. If you are replacing an old deck, photographs of the boards and the structure beneath are helpful. We assess what the new installation needs and make the preparation clear in the quotation.

sections.heading: Plan decking and a garden room together
paragraphs: A deck can extend the usable space outside a garden office, studio or room for relaxing. Planning the two together helps coordinate door positions, levels, seating and the route to your home. For features such as a hot tub or heavy equipment, tell us at the start so the relevant support requirements can be considered in the project design.

bullets: Steps and connections between garden levels
Decking alongside garden rooms and pergolas

faqs.q: Can you replace existing decking?
faqs.a: Yes. Send photos of the current deck, including any visible damage and the structure beneath where accessible. We will discuss removal, preparation and the specification for the replacement before quoting.

faqs.q: Which is better for my garden: timber or composite?
faqs.a: The best choice depends on the look you prefer, budget, product specification and care requirements. We can explain the options for your project so you can compare them on a clear basis.

faqs.q: Can the design include steps or a pergola?
faqs.a: Yes, these can be discussed as part of the project. Photos of the garden and approximate measurements help us understand the available space, changes in level and the kind of covered or open seating area you want.

faqs.q: What information do you need for a decking quote?
faqs.a: Your postcode, a few photos and approximate dimensions are a useful start. Tell us whether an existing deck needs removing, what you want to put on the deck and whether you have a preferred material or budget.

joinery.title: Bespoke Joinery in Colne & Lancashire | Tom Cutts
joinery.description: Bespoke joinery, fitted storage, media walls, doors and staircases in Colne and Lancashire. See Tom Cutts’ work and discuss your project with a free quote.
joinery.h1: Bespoke joinery, with care in every detail.
intro: Well-planned joinery makes a home easier to use and brings the details together. Tom Cutts Joinery & Building carries out bespoke joinery and carpentry across Colne, Pendle, the Ribble Valley and surrounding areas, from fitted storage and media walls to doors, staircases and the timber work within a larger build.

Tom’s 18+ years of hands-on and managerial experience spans both domestic properties and commercial sites. Whether you have one room in mind or need joinery throughout a renovation, we take time to understand the space, the finish and how the work fits into your wider plans.

sections.heading: Fitted storage that uses the space you have
paragraphs: Alcoves, awkward corners and the space beneath a staircase can all offer useful storage. Start with what you need to store: hanging clothes, books, everyday essentials or larger items. We can discuss the balance of shelves, cupboards and open space, then consider proportions, access and the finish in relation to the room.

sections.heading: Media walls, panelling and fitted features
paragraphs: A media wall should work with the equipment you own and the way you use the room. TV size, cable routes, shelving and any proposed electric fire need to be considered early. Decorative panelling and fitted features can also bring character to a hallway, bedroom or living space without losing sight of practical details.

sections.heading: Doors, staircases and the finishing work
paragraphs: Internal doors, skirting, architraves and window boards make a noticeable difference to the finished home. We also work on staircases and balustrades. Share photographs of the existing fittings and examples of the look you want, particularly where new joinery needs to sit alongside features you intend to keep.

sections.heading: Joinery as part of a bigger project
paragraphs: For extensions, renovations and commercial projects, joinery needs to be coordinated with the other work. We carry out first-fix work such as timber framing and studwork alongside second-fix finishing. Drawings, a specification and an outline programme help us discuss the scope, sequencing and the level of site support you need.

bullets: Fitted wardrobes, cupboards and alcove storage
Media walls and decorative wall panelling

faqs.q: Can you make fitted storage for an awkward space?
faqs.a: Yes. Send photographs, approximate dimensions and a description of what you want to store. We can discuss a layout that makes use of the available space and suits the surrounding room.

faqs.q: What is the difference between first- and second-fix joinery?
faqs.a: First-fix joinery generally covers timber work before plastering, such as studwork and door linings. Second-fix covers visible finishing work, including internal doors, skirting, architraves and other fitted details.

faqs.q: Can you build a media wall around my existing TV?
faqs.a: Yes, we can discuss a design around your equipment. Share the TV dimensions and details of any fire, speakers, shelving or lighting you want included so these can be considered together.

faqs.q: Do you take on commercial joinery projects?
faqs.a: Yes. Our work includes joinery for commercial fit-outs, developments and refurbishment projects. Send the drawings or scope, site location and proposed programme so we can discuss the support your project requires.

kitchens.title: Kitchen Fitters in Colne & Lancashire | Tom Cutts
kitchens.description: Kitchen fitting in Colne, Pendle and the Ribble Valley. Tom Cutts installs cabinetry, worktops and finishing details, with trade coordination. Get a quote.
kitchens.h1: Kitchen fitting that brings the whole room together.
intro: A new kitchen needs more than a good set of cabinets. The preparation, worktops, appliances and finishing details all need to fit together. Tom Cutts Joinery & Building provides kitchen installation across Colne, Pendle, the Ribble Valley and nearby areas, with the associated work discussed as part of the plan.

Whether you have already purchased your kitchen or are still deciding on the layout, we can help you understand the installation requirements. Tom brings 18+ years of joinery and building experience to the job, with clear communication about the scope and the trades involved.

sections.heading: Review the layout before installation
paragraphs: Bring your kitchen plan, cabinet schedule and appliance information to the conversation. We look at how the proposed layout relates to the room, existing services, doors and windows. Identifying preparation and installation requirements early helps you make informed decisions before delivery and gives the quotation a clearer basis.

sections.heading: Careful fitting, from cabinets to finishing details
paragraphs: Our kitchen work includes cabinet installation, worktop fitting, appliance integration and the joinery that completes the room. Alignment, trims, panels and the fit around existing walls all matter to the result. The worktop material and supplier requirements are discussed alongside the installation so the right arrangements are made for each part of the job.

sections.heading: Coordinate the associated trades
paragraphs: Moving a sink, changing the lighting or altering the layout can introduce work beyond the cabinetry. We can coordinate the plumbing, electrical work and other trades required for the agreed project. Responsibilities and the sequence of work should be clear at the start, particularly where you are supplying appliances or arranging part of the work yourself.

sections.heading: Make room for preparation and disruption
paragraphs: The existing kitchen may need removing, and walls or floors may require preparation before new units can be fitted. We discuss these tasks and how access to the room will work during the installation. If the kitchen forms part of an extension or wider renovation, we can consider it within the overall building programme.

faqs.q: Can you fit a kitchen I have already bought?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the kitchen plan, supplier details and appliance list so we can review the installation. Let us know the delivery arrangements and whether the existing kitchen still needs to be removed.

faqs.q: Can you coordinate plumbing and electrical work?
faqs.a: Yes, we can coordinate the associated trades as part of the agreed project. Tell us about changes to sinks, appliances, sockets and lighting so the work can be allowed for in the scope.

faqs.q: Can the kitchen installation include preparation work?
faqs.a: Yes. Removal of the old kitchen and preparation of walls or floors can be discussed. A site visit helps establish what is needed before the new kitchen can be installed.

faqs.q: How do I get an accurate kitchen-fitting quotation?
faqs.a: Provide the plan, dimensions, photographs, appliance details and your postcode. Tell us what you are supplying and any work you are arranging separately. We can then discuss the remaining details and quote for a clearly defined installation.

extensions.title: House Extensions in Colne & Lancashire | Tom Cutts
extensions.description: House extensions and garage conversions in Colne, Pendle and the Ribble Valley. Discuss your drawings, building work and project management with Tom Cutts.
extensions.h1: House extensions that make space for your next chapter.
intro: Create more room where you already feel at home. Tom Cutts Joinery & Building carries out house extensions and garage conversions across Colne, Pendle, the Ribble Valley and surrounding areas. We bring building work and joinery together, with the scope and project coordination discussed from the beginning.

Your priority might be a larger kitchen, another living area or a better connection to the garden. Tell us what the extra space needs to achieve. Tom’s experience across domestic building and commercial site management helps shape a practical conversation about the work involved.

sections.heading: Turn the idea into a clear building brief
paragraphs: We discuss the proposed use of the space, the existing house and how the extension will connect to it. Drawings, structural information and specifications help define the work and support a detailed quotation. If you are at an earlier stage, we can discuss what information is still needed before the build can be properly priced.

sections.heading: Consider the whole construction process
paragraphs: Groundworks, drainage, the structural shell, roofing and the internal finish are connected parts of an extension. Access and the condition of the existing property also influence the project. We work through the agreed scope so you understand the main stages and where specialist input, inspections and coordination will be required.

sections.heading: Plan the inside alongside the structure
paragraphs: The way a new room works depends on details such as door positions, lighting, kitchen layout and storage. Considering these early helps the structural work and services support the finished space. Our joinery background carries through to doors, skirting, cabinetry and the other details that help the extension feel part of your home.

sections.heading: A programme that recognises you live there
paragraphs: We discuss access, working areas and the points where the project will affect the existing house. Project management can include coordinating the trades involved in the agreed works and keeping you informed of progress. Changes to the scope should be discussed clearly, including their effect on the quotation and programme.

bullets: Building work, interior joinery and project coordination

faqs.q: Can I contact you before my drawings are complete?
faqs.a: Yes. We can discuss your ideas and the information needed to take the project forward. Detailed pricing will depend on the agreed design, specification and relevant structural information.

faqs.q: Do you carry out garage conversions?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us how you would like to use the space and send photographs of the garage and its connection to the house. We can discuss the work involved and the next steps for your project.

faqs.q: Can you manage the other trades involved?
faqs.a: Yes, project coordination can form part of the agreed service. We discuss the required trades, responsibilities and sequence of work so everyone understands how the build will be managed.

faqs.q: How long will an extension take?
faqs.a: The programme depends on the design, site conditions, materials and the scope of work. We discuss timing for your specific project after reviewing the relevant information, rather than applying one timescale to every extension.

renovations.title: Home Renovations in Lancashire | Tom Cutts
renovations.description: Home renovations and property refurbishment in Colne, Pendle and Lancashire. Discuss alterations, joinery and trade coordination with Tom Cutts. Free quotes.
renovations.h1: Home renovations, planned around the way you live.
intro: Improve the home you have with building work and joinery that belong together. Tom Cutts Joinery & Building undertakes renovations and property refurbishments in Colne, Pendle, the Ribble Valley and surrounding areas. We can discuss a single room, a series of improvements or a more extensive change to the property.

A renovation often involves several connected decisions: what to keep, what to change and which work needs doing first. Tom brings hands-on building experience and project management to that conversation, helping establish an agreed scope before work begins.

sections.heading: Start with the problems you want to solve
paragraphs: A cramped layout, limited storage or tired interiors each call for a different approach. Tell us what works in your home and what frustrates you. We can discuss the priorities, the rooms involved and how building alterations, kitchen fitting or bespoke joinery might fit into a practical programme of improvements.

sections.heading: Understand the building before changing it
paragraphs: Existing conditions affect both the scope and the order of renovation work. Where structural changes or specialist work are proposed, the relevant information needs to be established before that work begins. For older properties, we also discuss the features and materials you want to retain, drawing on our experience of heritage restoration.

sections.heading: Bring the trades and finishing details together
paragraphs: Renovations may involve preparation, building alterations, plumbing, electrical work, plastering and finishing joinery. We can coordinate the trades required for the agreed project and consider how one stage affects the next. Planning doors, skirting, storage and other fitted details early helps carry the intended finish through the whole job.

sections.heading: Keep the scope and communication clear
paragraphs: We discuss what is included, what you are arranging separately and how work will affect access to the property. A clear quotation helps you understand the agreed job. If the scope changes or opening up the building reveals an issue that needs attention, we discuss the implications before agreeing the next step with you.

bullets: Room improvements and wider property refurbishment
Doors, staircases, panelling and finishing joinery

faqs.q: Do you take on smaller renovation projects?
faqs.a: Yes, we can discuss individual rooms and specific improvements as well as wider refurbishments. Send a description of the work, photographs and your postcode so we can understand the project.

faqs.q: Can you work on an older property?
faqs.a: Our background includes heritage restoration. Tell us about the building, the work you have in mind and any known restrictions or specialist advice already obtained so we can discuss an appropriate scope.

faqs.q: Can the renovation be completed in stages?
faqs.a: We can discuss phasing where it suits the project. Some tasks depend on earlier work, so the proposed stages need to be considered together before agreeing a practical sequence.

faqs.q: What helps you prepare a renovation quotation?
faqs.a: A room-by-room list of priorities, photographs, your postcode and any drawings are useful. Include your preferred budget and timing, and let us know whether you expect to remain in the property while work takes place.

commercial.title: Commercial Joinery & Site Management | Tom Cutts
commercial.description: Commercial joinery, fit-outs and site management across Lancashire and the North West. Tom Cutts brings 18+ years’ experience. Discuss your project brief.
commercial.h1: Commercial joinery and site management, with detail in mind.
intro: Tom Cutts Joinery & Building supports commercial clients, developers and housing providers with joinery, building work and site project management across Lancashire and the wider North West. We discuss the scope, programme and responsibilities at the outset so the proposed service matches what your project needs.

Tom’s 18+ years of hands-on and managerial experience spans domestic and commercial construction. The business was established in 2020 and carries up to £5 million public liability insurance. Our background combines the practical demands of site work with the attention needed for the finished joinery.

sections.heading: Joinery for developments and refurbishments
paragraphs: We undertake first- and second-fix joinery within larger projects, from timber framing and studwork through to doors, skirting and fitted details. Drawings, schedules and specifications help define the work package. Tell us about the site arrangements, other trades and proposed sequence so these can be considered when discussing resources and timing.

sections.heading: Fit-outs shaped around the premises
paragraphs: Commercial interiors need to work for the people using them. Our fit-out work can include fitted storage, counters, shelving and staff kitchen areas. We discuss finishes and practical requirements alongside access, working areas and any constraints associated with occupied premises. The agreed brief should make clear which elements are included and which are being delivered by others.

sections.heading: Site coordination and project management
paragraphs: We offer site management alongside hands-on building and joinery services. The role can include coordinating trades, material requirements, progress and the quality of the agreed work. We establish the level of oversight required and the reporting arrangements with the client, including how decisions and changes will be communicated during the project.

sections.heading: Experience across public and private projects
paragraphs: Our experience includes work with Bury Council and Muir Housing, alongside private developments. Tom’s background also includes care-home builds and heritage restoration projects valued at over £1 million. For a new enquiry, tell us about the client requirements and the nature of the building so we can discuss the relevant experience and proposed approach.

bullets: Site project management and trade coordination

faqs.q: What information should we send with a commercial enquiry?
faqs.a: Send the site location, scope, drawings or specification, proposed programme and contact details for the person managing the enquiry. Include any site-access requirements and the date by which you need a response.

faqs.q: Can you provide joinery without managing the whole project?
faqs.a: Yes. We can discuss a defined joinery work package or a broader role that includes coordination and site management. Responsibilities are agreed around the needs of the project.

faqs.q: Which areas do you cover for commercial work?
faqs.a: We are based in Colne and undertake commercial work across Lancashire and the wider North West. Send the site postcode and an outline of the works so we can confirm suitability and availability.

faqs.q: Are you insured for commercial projects?
faqs.a: The business carries up to £5 million public liability insurance. Share your project’s insurance and documentation requirements during the enquiry so these can be reviewed against the proposed contract.
